In Chapter 2, @bali2016 summarize the distribution of stock characteristics within each year, then average those statistics across years.
This gives each year's cross-section equal weight.

## Implementation

### Periodic Cross-Sectional Summary Statistics {#annual-cross-sections}

The *methodologies sample* [@bali2016, sec. 1.1] covers US common stocks at each December 31 from 1988 through 2012.
I take the December value of the 12-month daily beta from @sec-bem-beta.
It uses all available daily excess returns in the calendar year and requires at least 200 matched observations.

```{python}
import polars as pl

from eap_pl import build_annual_panel, load_annual_betas

annual_beta = load_annual_betas().collect()
```

For each year, compute the statistics across the stocks with a beta.
I use the sample standard deviation, bias-adjusted skewness and excess kurtosis, and linearly interpolated percentiles.
The count is the number of available values in that cross-section.

```{python}
def cross_section(variable):
    x = pl.col(variable)
    return [
        x.mean().alias("Mean"),
        x.std().alias("SD"),
        x.skew(bias=False).alias("Skew"),
        x.kurtosis(fisher=True, bias=False).alias("Kurt."),
        x.min().alias("Min"),
        x.quantile(.05, interpolation="linear").alias("5%"),
        x.quantile(.25, interpolation="linear").alias("25%"),
        x.median().alias("Median"),
        x.quantile(.75, interpolation="linear").alias("75%"),
        x.quantile(.95, interpolation="linear").alias("95%"),
        x.max().alias("Max"),
        x.count().alias("n"),
    ]

annual_stats = (
    annual_beta.group_by("year")
    .agg(cross_section("Beta"))
    .sort("year")
)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem2-annual
#| tbl-cap: Annual summary statistics for market beta (BEM Table 2.1)
#| code-fold: true

annual_stats.rename({"year": "Year"}).eap.show_table()
```

### Average Cross-Sectional Summary Statistics {#average-across-years}

To describe the typical cross-section, take the mean of each column in @tbl-bem2-annual.
For example, if $n_t$ stocks have valid betas in year $t$, their mean is $\bar{\beta}_t = \sum_{i=1}^{n_t}\widehat{\beta}_{i,t}/n_t$.
The table reports $T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\bar{\beta}_t$.
A pooled mean would instead give years with more observations more weight.
The same two-step procedure applies to the median and other statistics.

```{python}
average_stats = annual_stats.select(pl.exclude("year").mean())
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem2-average
#| tbl-cap: Average cross-sectional summary statistics for market beta (BEM Table 2.2)
#| code-fold: true

average_stats.with_columns(pl.col("n").round().cast(pl.Int64)).eap.show_table()
```

The annual table also shows that mean beta increased from 0.46 in 1988 to 1.04 in 2012.
The time-series average hides that change.

## Presentation and Interpretation {#sec-summary-characteristics}

[]{#summarize-several-characteristics}I also summarize year-end market capitalization in millions of dollars, its natural logarithm (size), book-to-market, and the following calendar year's excess return.
`build_annual_panel()` assembles these observations using `start_year` and `end_year`, which default to 1988 and 2012.

{{< include _show-code.qmd >}}

The December beta observations already calculated for @tbl-bem2-annual define the stock-years in the panel.
The helper uses `permno` and formation year as the join keys.
`build_sizes()` provides December market capitalization and its log, as described in @sec-size-replication.
`build_book_to_market()` supplies the ratio of prior-year fiscal book equity to prior December market capitalization, as described in @sec-value-replication.
I use its signed ratio, consistent with the negative observations in BEM Table 2.3.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

show_code(build_annual_panel, "betas", "keys", "sizes", "capitalizations", "book_to_market")
```

For each stock and holding year, the helper compounds the available monthly returns reported by CRSP.
BEM §1.1 does not spell out how its annual returns handle delistings.
The helper compounds the monthly risk-free returns separately, requiring 12 observations for the year.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

show_code(build_annual_panel, "stock_returns", "risk_free")
```

Subtract the annual risk-free return from the stock return and express the difference in percentage points.
Subtracting one from the holding year aligns the return with the characteristics measured the preceding December.
For example, the return earned in 1989 is joined to the stock's 1988 characteristics.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

show_code(build_annual_panel, "next_year")
```

The left joins keep each stock-year in the beta sample even when a characteristic or return is missing.
`end_year` is both the last formation year and the last calendar year included in the return calculations.
In the default sample, this leaves the 2012 formation rows with missing next-year returns.
The final `.collect()` returns the assembled panel as a Polars `DataFrame`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

show_code(build_annual_panel, "return")
```

```{python}
annual_panel = build_annual_panel(annual_betas=annual_beta)
```

Apply the same summary to each variable separately.
This keeps stocks with a beta but no book-to-market ratio in the beta row.
The observation count reflects the available data for each variable.

```{python}
variables = ["Beta", "MktCap", "Size", "BM", "excess"]
all_stats = (
    annual_panel.unpivot(on=variables, index="year", variable_name="Measure")
    .group_by("year", "Measure")
    .agg(cross_section("value"))
    .group_by("Measure")
    .agg(pl.exclude("year", "Measure").mean())
)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem2-characteristics
#| tbl-cap: Average annual summary statistics for stock characteristics and next-year returns (BEM Table 2.3)
#| code-fold: true

table_2_3 = (
    pl.DataFrame({"Measure": variables}).join(all_stats, on="Measure", maintain_order="left")
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("n").round().cast(pl.Int64),
        pl.col("Measure").replace({
            "MktCap": "Market cap", "BM": "Book-to-market", "excess": "Next-year excess return (%)",
        }),
    )
)
table_2_3.eap.show_table()
```

Market capitalization has a long right tail.
In @tbl-bem2-characteristics, the mean is about $2 billion while the median is about $188 million.
Taking logs reduces skewness.
The annual mean excess return averages 12.40%, and the annual median averages about 0.90%.

```{python}
#| include: false

from polars.testing import assert_frame_equal

assert annual_stats["year"].to_list() == list(range(1988, 2013))
assert annual_panel.filter(pl.col("year") == 2012)["excess"].is_null().all()
assert annual_panel.filter(pl.col("excess").is_not_null())["year"].n_unique() == 24
assert_frame_equal(
    table_2_3.head(1).drop("Measure"),
    average_stats.with_columns(pl.col("n").round().cast(pl.Int64)),
)
```
